title: Pandas
test_conventions: Tests are Python assert snippets run AFTER the learner's code in the same namespace. The learner's stdout is available to tests as the string variable __stdout__. expected_output comparisons are exact after stripping trailing whitespace on each line. Tests with visible:false are hidden and each carries a failure_message. Everything runs offline in Pyodide; no input(), network or pip. The learner's own source code is also available to tests as the string variable __source__ (use it for AST/source checks that catch hard-coded answers).

exercises.code:

data = [{'Name': 'Asabeneh', 'Country': 'Finland'},
        {'Name': 'David', 'Country': 'UK'}]

misconceptions.(1, 4) ['Name', 'Country'] ['Finland', ': Each dict becomes one row, so there are 2 rows and 2 columns.

exercises.prompt: In your own words: what is the difference between a pandas Series and a DataFrame?
exercises.prompt_tr: Kendi cümlelerinle anlat: pandas Series ile DataFrame arasındaki fark nedir?
exercises.model_answer: A Series is a single column of data with an index. A DataFrame is a table made of several Series that share the same index, so it has rows and many named columns. Selecting one column of a DataFrame gives you a Series.
exercises.model_answer_tr: Series, indeksi olan tek bir veri sütunudur. DataFrame ise aynı indeksi paylaşan birkaç Series'ten oluşan bir tablodur; yani satırları ve adlandırılmış birçok sütunu vardır. Bir DataFrame'in tek bir sütununu seçersen bir Series elde edersin.

exercises.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
csv = 'Gender,Height,Weight\nMale,73,241\nFemale,63,128\nMale,69,206\nFemale,66,170'
df = pd.read_csv(StringIO(csv))
print(df.shape, df.head(2)['Gender'].tolist(), df.tail(1)['Weight'].tolist())
exercises.explanation: The CSV has a header and 4 data rows with 3 columns, so shape is (4, 3). head(2) takes the first two genders; tail(1) takes the last row, whose Weight is 170.

misconceptions.(3, 4) ['Male', 'Female'] [170]: shape is (rows, columns). There are 4 rows and 3 columns.
misconceptions.(4, 3) ['Male', 'Female'] [241]: tail(1) is the LAST row (Weight 170). 241 is in the first row.
misconceptions.(4, 3) ['Male', 'Male'] [170]: head(2) takes the first two rows: Male then Female.

exercises.explanation_tr: CSV'de bir başlık ve 3 sütunlu 4 veri satırı var, yani shape (4, 3). head(2) ilk iki cinsiyeti alır; tail(1) son satırı alır ve onun Weight değeri 170'tir.

misconceptions_tr.(3, 4) ['Male', 'Female'] [170]: shape (satır, sütun) demektir. 4 satır ve 3 sütun var.
misconceptions_tr.(4, 3) ['Male', 'Male'] [170]: head(2) ilk iki satırı alır: önce Male, sonra Female.

exercises.code:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.DataFrame({'Name': ['A', 'B'], 'Birth Year': ['1990', '1985']})
df['Birth Year'] = df['Birth Year'].astype('int')
df['Age'] = 2020 - df['Birth Year']
print(df['Age'].tolist(), df.columns.tolist())
exercises.explanation: astype('int') turns the year strings into integers, so 2020 - year works: 30 and 35. The new Age column is added after the existing ones.

misconceptions.[30, 35] ['Name', 'Age']: Assigning to df['Age'] adds a column; Birth Year is still there.
misconceptions.[1990, 1985] ['Name', 'Birth Year', 'Age: Age is 2020 minus the year, not the year itself.
misconceptions.Error: The strings were converted to int first, so the subtraction is valid.

exercises.explanation_tr: astype('int') yıl metinlerini tam sayıya çevirir, böylece 2020 - yıl işlemi çalışır: 30 ve 35. Yeni Age sütunu mevcutların sonuna eklenir.

misconceptions_tr.[30, 35] ['Name', 'Age']: df['Age']'e atama sütun ekler; Birth Year yerinde kalır.
misconceptions_tr.[1990, 1985] ['Name', 'Birth Year', 'Age: Age, yılın kendisi değil, 2020 eksi yıldır.
misconceptions_tr.Error: Metinler önce int'e çevrildi, bu yüzden çıkarma işlemi geçerlidir.

solution.approach: Filter with a boolean mask built from the chosen column.
solution.code:
def rows_above(df, column, limit):
    return df[df[column] > limit]
